resort to verb

also have recourse to, fall back on, turn to (for help), take refuge in

classical

Cic. Lig. 30: ad clēmentiam tuam (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 6.1.4: ad precēs

cōnfugiō, cōnfugere, cōnfūgī

verb, third conjugation (-iō); ad + accusative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

resort to, have recourse to, take refuge in

Literally to flee for refuge; figuratively, and often in Cicero, to fall back on a means: entreaties, someone’s mercy, philosophy.

Examples

  • Cum nihil aliud prōdesset, ad precēs cōnfūgit.

    When nothing else worked, he resorted to begging.composed

See also extreme, escape, help.

SourcesLewis & Short: confugio

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
